name: Notifier
doc:
# Notifier Module

The Notifier module provides a complete **event-driven notification system** with user preferences and flexible delivery options.

## Key Features

- **Event-driven notifications** - Other modules can emit events to create notifications via the `notifier.call.create` event
- **Snooze functionality** - Users can postpone notifications (default: 7 days)
- **Dismiss permanently** - Users can dismiss notifications they don't want to see again
- **User preferences** - Users can configure which event types trigger notifications
- **Toast UI** - Notifications displayed as toasts with customizable duration (2 minutes)
- **Polling system** - Frontend polls for new notifications every 30 seconds
- **Multi-tenant** - Domain-scoped notifications for multi-tenancy support

## Notification Lifecycle

1. A notification is created (via API or event) with status `pending`
2. When the frontend polls, pending notifications are returned and auto-marked as `shown`
3. The user can **dismiss** (permanent) or **snooze** (temporary, re-appears after N days)
4. Snoozed notifications return to the pending queue once `snooze_until` has passed

## Notification Types

Four UI styling types: `info` (blue), `success` (green), `warning` (yellow), `error` (red).

## Event Types

Event types are arbitrary strings defined by consuming modules. Common examples:
- `user.login`, `user.password_expiring`
- `comment.mention`, `comment.reply`
- `system.maintenance`, `system.update`
- `gdpr.expiring`, `license.expiring`

## Inter-Module Integration

Other modules create notifications by calling the `notifier.call.create` event:

```typescript
await liwe_event_call(app, 'notifier.create', {
  id_user: user.id,
  event_type: 'comment.mention',
  title: 'You were mentioned',
  message: 'Someone mentioned you in a comment',
  notification_type: 'info',
  data: { id_comment: comment.id },
  domain: user.domain
});
```

## Configuration Defaults

- **Polling interval**: 30 seconds
- **Toast duration**: 2 minutes (120 seconds)
- **Default snooze period**: 7 days

endp.notifier.add.description:
## Create a New Notification

Creates a new notification for a specific user. The notification is stored with `pending` status and will be delivered on the next frontend polling cycle.

### Behavior

- The notification `status` is automatically set to `pending`
- The `created` and `updated` timestamps are set to the current time
- A unique `id` is auto-generated for the notification
- The `domain` is inherited from the authenticated user's context
- After creation, the `notifier.created` event is emitted

### Notification Types

| Type | UI Style | Use Case |
|------|----------|----------|
| `info` | Blue | General information |
| `success` | Green | Positive confirmation |
| `warning` | Yellow | Caution or expiring items |
| `error` | Red | Critical alerts |

If `notification_type` is omitted, it defaults to `info`.

### The `data` Field

The optional `data` parameter accepts arbitrary JSON for passing extra context to the frontend (e.g., IDs for deep linking, counts, metadata).

### Example Request Body

```json
{
  "id_user": "usr_abc123",
  "event_type": "comment.mention",
  "title": "You were mentioned",
  "message": "John mentioned you in a comment",
  "notification_type": "info",
  "data": { "id_comment": "cmt_456" }
}
```

parameters.name: id_user
parameters.description: User ID who should receive the notification

parameters.name: event_type
parameters.description: Event type that triggered this notification

endp.notifier.list.description:
## Get Pending Notifications

Retrieves the list of actionable notifications for the currently authenticated user. This endpoint is designed for **frontend polling** (default: every 30 seconds).

### Selection Criteria

A notification is returned if it matches **any** of these conditions:
- Status is `pending` (never shown to the user yet)
- Status is `snoozed` **and** `snooze_until` timestamp has passed (snooze expired)

Notifications with status `dismissed` or `shown` are **never** returned.

### Side Effects

- All returned notifications are automatically updated to `shown` status
- The `updated` timestamp is refreshed for each returned notification

### Ordering & Limits

- Results are ordered by `created` date (newest first)
- The `limit` query parameter controls the maximum number of results (default: 10)

### Example Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "ntf_abc123",
      "id_user": "usr_xyz",
      "event_type": "comment.mention",
      "title": "New Comment",
      "message": "You were mentioned in a comment",
      "status": "pending",
      "notification_type": "info",
      "data": { "id_comment": "cmt_456" },
      "domain": "mydomain",
      "created": "2026-03-13T10:00:00Z",
      "updated": "2026-03-13T10:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of notifications to return

endp.notifier.dismiss.description:
## Dismiss a Notification

Permanently dismisses a notification. Once dismissed, the notification will **never** be returned by the `/notifier/list` endpoint again.

### Behavior

- Sets the notification `status` to `dismissed`
- Updates the `updated` timestamp
- Emits the `notifier.dismissed` event with the notification data
- The notification remains in the database for audit purposes but is excluded from all queries

### Authorization

- The user can only dismiss notifications belonging to them (`id_user` must match the authenticated user)
- Returns `false` if the notification does not exist or does not belong to the user

### Example Request Body

```json
{
  "id": "ntf_abc123"
}
```

### Returns

`true` if the notification was successfully dismissed, `false` otherwise.

endp.notifier.snooze.description:
## Snooze a Notification

Temporarily hides a notification for a specified number of days. After the snooze period expires, the notification will reappear in the `/notifier/list` results.

### Behavior

- Sets the notification `status` to `snoozed`
- Calculates `snooze_until` as the current time plus the specified number of days
- Updates the `updated` timestamp
- Emits the `notifier.snoozed` event with the notification data

### Snooze Expiration

When the `snooze_until` timestamp passes, the notification is automatically picked up again by the `/notifier/list` endpoint. No background job is required - the list query checks for expired snoozes at read time.

### Authorization

- The user can only snooze notifications belonging to them (`id_user` must match the authenticated user)

### Example Request Body

```json
{
  "id": "ntf_abc123",
  "days": 14
}
```

### Returns

The `snooze_until` Unix timestamp indicating when the notification will reappear:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "snooze_until": 1742342400
}
```

endp.notifier.settings.delete.description:
## Delete a Notification Setting

Deletes a notification preference setting by ID. Only the owner of the setting can delete it.

### Behavior

- Verifies the setting exists and belongs to the authenticated user
- Removes the `NotificationSetting` record from the database
- Returns `true` on successful deletion
- Returns 404 if the setting does not exist or does not belong to the user

### Authorization

- The user can only delete settings belonging to them (`id_user` must match the authenticated user)
- Domain scoping is enforced

### Example Request Body

```json
{
  "id": "nts_abc123"
}
```

### Returns

`true` if the setting was successfully deleted.

endp.notifier.settings.get.description:
## Get Notification Settings

Retrieves the notification preference settings for the currently authenticated user. Returns a list of event types the user has configured, along with their enabled/disabled state.

### Behavior

- Returns all `NotificationSetting` records matching the current user's `id_user` and `domain`
- If the user has never configured any settings, an empty array is returned
- Event types not present in the response are considered **enabled by default** (opt-out model)

### Use Case

This endpoint powers the notification preferences UI where users can toggle which event types they want to receive notifications for (e.g., disable `comment.mention` but keep `system.maintenance`).

### Example Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "nst_abc123",
      "id_user": "usr_xyz",
      "event_type": "comment.mention",
      "enabled": true,
      "domain": "mydomain"
    },
    {
      "id": "nst_def456",
      "id_user": "usr_xyz",
      "event_type": "system.maintenance",
      "enabled": false,
      "domain": "mydomain"
    }
  ]
}
```

endp.notifier.settings.update.description:
## Update Notification Setting

Creates or updates a notification preference for a specific event type. Allows users to opt in or out of notifications for individual event types.

### Behavior

- If a setting for the given `event_type` already exists for the user, it is **updated** (upsert)
- If no setting exists, a new `NotificationSetting` record is **created**
- The `domain` is inherited from the authenticated user's context
- When `enabled` is set to `false`, future notifications of that `event_type` will **not** be created for this user

### Opt-Out Model

The system uses an **opt-out** model: all event types are enabled by default. Users explicitly disable the ones they do not want. Setting `enabled: true` restores the default behavior.

### Example Request Body

```json
{
  "event_type": "comment.mention",
  "enabled": false
}
```

### Example Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "id": "nst_abc123",
    "id_user": "usr_xyz",
    "event_type": "comment.mention",
    "enabled": false,
    "domain": "mydomain"
  }
}
```

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: Whether to enable or disable notifications for this event type
